frames.narration: A build finishes an image with 12 layers. For each layer the CI job sends a HEAD request with its digest. The registry has 11 of them already, since they are shared base and library layers, so only one layer, 38 MB, needs to be sent.
The CI job opens an upload session and sends the new layer in 8 MB chunks, each tagged with its offset. The network drops after three chunks, 24 MB.

The job reconnects and asks where the upload stands. The session answers 24 MB, so the job sends only the remaining 14 MB. A repeat of an old chunk would be refused because its offset no longer matches.
The final request names the digest the job expects. The server hashes all 38 MB, sees that it matches, and only then publishes the blob under that digest. A mismatch would discard the upload.

The job pushes the manifest, which lists the config and the 12 layer digests. The registry checks that all 13 blobs exist, stores the manifest by its own digest, and moves the tag app:v7 to it in the metadata database.

The push triggers a scan. The scanner reads the layers, finds no critical vulnerabilities, and records the report against the digest. The pipeline signs the digest, and the signature is stored beside the image as a small artifact.
A replication job sends the manifest to region B along with only the layers that region does not have. Region B verifies every digest and publishes the tag only when the whole image is there.

A server in region B is told to run app@sha256:c41e... It already holds 10 of the 12 layers, so it fetches the manifest, checks the signature and the scan result, and downloads two layers from a signed URL in its own region. It hashes each one before it uses it.

That night the collector marks every digest reachable from a tag and sweeps unreferenced blobs older than the grace period of 2 hours, which is longer than any push plus one collection run. The layers of a push that began 10 minutes ago are untouched.
